2.1 The Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone (BBRZ) shall comprise the following administrative units:

a) Bhuj Taluka: Full extent, including all gram panchayats, villages, and municipal wards falling under the Bhuj Municipality and Bhuj Taluka Panchayat. Specific villages include, but are not limited to: Bhujodi, Madhapar, Kukma, Mirjapur, Lakhond, Kotay, and the urban areas of Bhuj city.

b) Bhachau Taluka: Full extent, including all gram panchayats, villages, and municipal areas under the Bhachau Taluka Panchayat and Bhachau Municipality. Specific villages include, but are not limited to: Bhachau town, Chobari, Gandhar, Rapar (only the western revenue villages of Rapar Taluka that fall within the Bhachau sub-division), Samakhiyali, and surrounding settlements.

2.2 For the purpose of operational clarity, the boundary of BBRZ shall be considered as co-terminus with the revenue boundaries of Bhuj Taluka and the western half of Bhachau Taluka, as per the latest land revenue records available with the District Inspector of Land Records (DILR), Kutch. Any dispute regarding the exact boundary of a village or ward shall be resolved by the Deputy Collector (Revenue) in consultation with the BBRZ Shelter Coordinator.

2.3 A map showing the designated boundaries is annexed to the Gujarati version of this order and is available in the DEOC control room for inspection. The map is for guidance only; the revenue records shall be the final authority for boundary determination.

3. OFFICIAL ZONE CODE

3.1 For the purpose of identification in all official correspondence, data systems, logistics tracking, and situation reports, the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone (BBRZ) shall be known by its official zone code.

3.2 In the Kutch DEOC order, the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone official_zone_code is listed as BRZ-04. Record status: current. This code is the current and valid designation for all reporting and resource allocation purposes.

3.3 All agencies, departments, and personnel operating within the BBRZ shall use the code "BRZ-04" in the subject line of all written communications, in the header of all data entry forms, and in the field designated for "Zone" in the daily situation report (SITREP) format. Use of any other code, such as the interim codes assigned in Order No. 09/2025 (e.g., "Zone-4A" or "BBZ"), shall be discontinued immediately and shall not be used in any new records after the date of this order. Historical records may retain their old codes for archival reference, but all new entries must reflect BRZ-04.

3.4 The code BRZ-04 is also to be used in the common operational picture (COP) software and the GIS-based dashboard maintained by the DEOC. The IT Cell has been instructed to update the zone nomenclature in the system by 18:00 hours today, 04/12/2025.

4. DELEGATION OF AUTHORITY

4.1 In accordance with the powers vested in me, and in the interest of efficient and timely response, I hereby delegate the following authority to the District Shelter Coordinator for the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone:

4.2 The District Shelter Coordinator, Kutch (hereinafter referred to as DSC-BBRZ) shall be responsible for the overall management, coordination, and supervision of all emergency shelters within the BBRZ. This includes, but is not limited to:

a) Approval of new shelter sites and de-notification of existing shelters, in consultation with the concerned Mamlatdar and the local municipality/panchayat.

b) Allocation of resources, including food packets, drinking water, blankets, tarpaulin sheets, and hygiene kits, to individual shelters based on the daily census data.

In continuation of the aforementioned order, the following additional provisions, responsibilities, and reporting protocols are hereby notified for the smooth and effective functioning of the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone (BBRZ), now officially designated as BRZ-04.

5. ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF EMERGENCY SHELTERS

5.1 The DSC-BBRZ shall ensure that all emergency shelters within the zone are established and managed in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Shelter Management, issued by the Gujarat State Disaster Management Authority (GSDMA) vide letter No. GSDMA/SOP/Shelter/2025/118 dated 15/11/2025, and subsequent amendments.

5.2 The following categories of shelters shall be established, as per the needs assessment and site suitability survey conducted by the Revenue Department and the District Development Office:

a) Primary Shelters (PS): Large-capacity shelters located in community buildings, schools, and other public structures capable of housing 200 or more displaced persons. These shall be the primary points for distribution of relief material and provision of basic services.

b) Secondary Shelters (SS): Smaller shelters, typically accommodating 50-200 persons, established in panchayat halls, community centers, or other suitable structures in areas where the affected population is scattered.

c) Transit Shelters (TS): Temporary staging points near the affected areas or along evacuation routes, providing short-term accommodation (maximum 72 hours) and basic first aid before persons are moved to Primary or Secondary Shelters.

5.3 The DSC-BBRZ shall, in consultation with the Mamlatdar of Bhuj and Bhachau talukas, identify and designate the specific buildings/structures to be used as shelters. The list of designated shelters, along with their capacity and location details, shall be submitted to the DEOC within 72 hours of the issuance of this order.

5.4 No shelter shall be opened without prior approval of the DSC-BBRZ. In urgent cases, the Shelter In-Charge may open a shelter and simultaneously report the same to the DSC-BBRZ within 2 hours. The DSC-BBRZ shall either approve the opening or order the closure/relocation of the shelter within 24 hours of such report.

5.5 The DSC-BBRZ shall ensure that each shelter has a designated Shelter In-Charge, who shall be a government employee (preferably from the Revenue, Education, or Health Department) and shall be responsible for:

a) Day-to-day management of the shelter, including registration of inmates, maintenance of attendance, and upkeep of the premises.

b) Coordination with the taluka-level relief teams for supply of food, water, and other essential items.

c) Reporting to the DSC-BBRZ through the designated reporting channel on a daily basis, as per the format prescribed in the SOPs.

d) Ensuring that all inmates are treated with dignity and respect, and that the shelter is a safe and secure environment, especially for women, children, elderly, and persons with disabilities.

documents.content:
2.1 The Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone (BBRZ) shall comprise the following administrative units:

a) Bhuj Taluka: Full extent, including all gram panchayats, villages, and municipal wards falling under the Bhuj Municipality and Bhuj Taluka Panchayat. Specific villages include, but are not limited to: Bhujodi, Madhapar, Kukma, Mirjapur, Lakhond, Kotay, and the urban areas of Bhuj city.

b) Bhachau Taluka: Full extent, including all gram panchayats, villages, and municipal areas under the Bhachau Taluka Panchayat and Bhachau Municipality. Specific villages include, but are not limited to: Bhachau town, Chobari, Gandhar, Rapar (only the western revenue villages of Rapar Taluka that fall within the Bhachau sub-division), Samakhiyali, and surrounding settlements.

2.2 For the purpose of operational clarity, the boundary of BBRZ shall be considered as co-terminus with the revenue boundaries of Bhuj Taluka and the western half of Bhachau Taluka, as per the latest land revenue records available with the District Inspector of Land Records (DILR), Kutch. Any dispute regarding the exact boundary of a village or ward shall be resolved by the Deputy Collector (Revenue) in consultation with the BBRZ Shelter Coordinator.

2.3 A map showing the designated boundaries is annexed to the Gujarati version of this order and is available in the DEOC control room for inspection. The map is for guidance only; the revenue records shall be the final authority for boundary determination.

3. OFFICIAL ZONE CODE

3.1 For the purpose of identification in all official correspondence, data systems, logistics tracking, and situation reports, the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone (BBRZ) shall be known by its official zone code.

3.2 In the Kutch DEOC order, the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone official_zone_code is listed as BRZ-04. Record status: current. This code is the current and valid designation for all reporting and resource allocation purposes.

3.3 All agencies, departments, and personnel operating within the BBRZ shall use the code "BRZ-04" in the subject line of all written communications, in the header of all data entry forms, and in the field designated for "Zone" in the daily situation report (SITREP) format. Use of any other code, such as the interim codes assigned in Order No. 09/2025 (e.g., "Zone-4A" or "BBZ"), shall be discontinued immediately and shall not be used in any new records after the date of this order. Historical records may retain their old codes for archival reference, but all new entries must reflect BRZ-04.

3.4 The code BRZ-04 is also to be used in the common operational picture (COP) software and the GIS-based dashboard maintained by the DEOC. The IT Cell has been instructed to update the zone nomenclature in the system by 18:00 hours today, 04/12/2025.

4. DELEGATION OF AUTHORITY

4.1 In accordance with the powers vested in me, and in the interest of efficient and timely response, I hereby delegate the following authority to the District Shelter Coordinator for the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone:

4.2 The District Shelter Coordinator, Kutch (hereinafter referred to as DSC-BBRZ) shall be responsible for the overall management, coordination, and supervision of all emergency shelters within the BBRZ. This includes, but is not limited to:

a) Approval of new shelter sites and de-notification of existing shelters, in consultation with the concerned Mamlatdar and the local municipality/panchayat.

b) Allocation of resources, including food packets, drinking water, blankets, tarpaulin sheets, and hygiene kits, to individual shelters based on the daily census data.

Subject: Designation of Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone and Delegation of Authority – Continuation of Order No. 12/2025 issued 04/12/2025.

In continuation of the aforementioned order, the following additional provisions, responsibilities, and reporting protocols are hereby notified for the smooth and effective functioning of the Bhuj-Bhachau Relief Zone (BBRZ), now officially designated as BRZ-04.

5. ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT OF EMERGENCY SHELTERS

5.1 The DSC-BBRZ shall ensure that all emergency shelters within the zone are established and managed in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Shelter Management, issued by the Gujarat State Disaster Management Authority (GSDMA) vide letter No. GSDMA/SOP/Shelter/2025/118 dated 15/11/2025, and subsequent amendments.

5.2 The following categories of shelters shall be established, as per the needs assessment and site suitability survey conducted by the Revenue Department and the District Development Office:

a) Primary Shelters (PS): Large-capacity shelters located in community buildings, schools, and other public structures capable of housing 200 or more displaced persons. These shall be the primary points for distribution of relief material and provision of basic services.

b) Secondary Shelters (SS): Smaller shelters, typically accommodating 50-200 persons, established in panchayat halls, community centers, or other suitable structures in areas where the affected population is scattered.

c) Transit Shelters (TS): Temporary staging points near the affected areas or along evacuation routes, providing short-term accommodation (maximum 72 hours) and basic first aid before persons are moved to Primary or Secondary Shelters.

5.3 The DSC-BBRZ shall, in consultation with the Mamlatdar of Bhuj and Bhachau talukas, identify and designate the specific buildings/structures to be used as shelters. The list of designated shelters, along with their capacity and location details, shall be submitted to the DEOC within 72 hours of the issuance of this order.

5.4 No shelter shall be opened without prior approval of the DSC-BBRZ. In urgent cases, the Shelter In-Charge may open a shelter and simultaneously report the same to the DSC-BBRZ within 2 hours. The DSC-BBRZ shall either approve the opening or order the closure/relocation of the shelter within 24 hours of such report.

5.5 The DSC-BBRZ shall ensure that each shelter has a designated Shelter In-Charge, who shall be a government employee (preferably from the Revenue, Education, or Health Department) and shall be responsible for:

a) Day-to-day management of the shelter, including registration of inmates, maintenance of attendance, and upkeep of the premises.

b) Coordination with the taluka-level relief teams for supply of food, water, and other essential items.

c) Reporting to the DSC-BBRZ through the designated reporting channel on a daily basis, as per the format prescribed in the SOPs.

d) Ensuring that all inmates are treated with dignity and respect, and that the shelter is a safe and secure environment, especially for women, children, elderly, and persons with disabilities.
